label: Logical falsity, from the factive CausesIn set under adopted POTENCY_1 (inference)
rule: Instantiate the observation, take a mover, apply the two CausesIn premises, and contradict the adopted potency of the moved thing
meaning: Under adopted POTENCY_1 (InPotency x r := CanBe x r ∧ ¬ InAct x r), with one MovedIn, MovesIn, CausesIn and InAct: something x is being moved in some respect r (fbc516c1); some y moves x in r (6b9fedc2, whose in-act clause is not used); y then causes x's being r (6a0b545c, the explicit bridge from moving, CAUSE_1, to causing a perfection, CAUSE_2); so x is in act in r (67aa5b5c); but x, being moved in r, is in POTENCY_1 in r (4be9a4ac), hence not in act in r. The five premises therefore cannot all hold under one interpretation of CausesIn and InAct; the derivation is constructive. It certifies lane A's 2026-11-18 finding: 6a0b545c needs a non-factive, in-progress reading of CausesIn, or the routes through 6a0b545c (892db443) and through 67aa5b5c (90e85f77, f632c6e5) need distinct relations. It does not select which member to reject. Under adopted POTENCY_1 the non-overlap premise c6d6379b is definitional and is not a member. On the generic vocabulary with an independent InPotency, the six-member set with c6d6379b is the same derivation, but c6d6379b carries POTENCY_2 while 4be9a4ac carries POTENCY_1, so one argument over that set would need a registered POTENCY_1/POTENCY_2 sense bridge; none is registered and none is introduced here. The closed controls causesInControls give, for each of the five members, a Bool/Unit interpretation under adopted potency in which the other four hold and that member fails, so the core is inclusion-minimal in this vocabulary (facts about those interpretations only, not registered models).
